name: Chamomilla
origin: Europe and western Asia; naturalised and cultivated widely
habitat: Cultivated fields, roadsides and waste ground in temperate regions
partUsed: Whole fresh plant in flower (flower heads)
preparation: Mother tincture and attenuations prepared from the fresh flowering plant according to traditional homeopathic pharmacopoeial methods
chemicalConstituents: Volatile oil containing chamazulene and alpha-bisabolol
generalAnalysis: A plant remedy whose guiding symptoms belong chiefly to the mind and emotions. It is used traditionally for states of extreme oversensitiveness, especially in children, where pain feels unbearable and provokes irritability, anger and inconsolable crying. The classical picture includes one cheek red and hot while the other is pale and cold, a child quiet only while being carried, and a dry cough at night during sleep.

drugPicture.generalPicture: A picture of intolerance of pain. The patient, often a teething child, is peevish, impatient and angry; the pain seems unendurable and is accompanied by numbness. The child cries until carried, asks for things and then refuses them, and may have one cheek red and hot while the other is pale and cold.
